chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the contracted slave (mukatab). He said: 'What you stipulated upon him is valid/permissible upon him.'

key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبِ: A slave who has contracted with his master to pay a certain sum for his freedom.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on the stipulations made in a slave's contract of manumission (kitabah)?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi affirms the principle of contractual freedom (istihsan) in Islamic jurisprudence, validating that the specific terms agreed upon for a slave's manumission (kitabah) are legally binding. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the master's stipulations define the scope of the slave's obligation, reflecting the practical application of mutual consent in commercial and social transactions.
